title: Hardship Determinations and the Appointment Series No-Show Fee
content:
Financial Assistance Office questions and answers on the no-show fee of an Appointment Series for patients in the Patient Hardship Discount Program.

**Rule.** The no-show hardship share is 0 percent where the patient holds an approved hardship determination whose effective date has arrived and whose expiry date has not passed at a level whose discount percentage is 75 or more, 100 percent less the level's discount percentage where such an approved determination in force discounts more than zero but less than 75 percent, and 100 percent where no approved determination is in force. The share is read as a percentage of the no-show basis and multiplies it.

**What makes a determination in force?** It is approved, its effective date is on or before the assessment date and its expiry date is on or after it. On the expiry date itself it is still in force.

**Which records are read?** The patient's Patient Hardship Discount Program determination: status, effective date, expiry date and the discount percentage of its level.

**A determination in force at a level discounting 75 percent — what share?** 0 percent, as for any level discounting 75 percent or more.

**At a level discounting 25 percent?** 100 percent less 25 percent, that is 75 percent.

**A determination that expired the day before the assessment, or one still only applied for?** No approved determination is in force: 100 percent.

**Example (hypothetical figures).** A level discounting 50 percent, on a no-show basis of USD 65.00: 50 percent of USD 65.00 is USD 32.50.
